text: This is Lunar Site Planner. In under two minutes, I'll show you how to plan a Moon landing in Professional mode, from picking a site to sharing a report.
On the left is your mission flow: five steps, in order. The 3D Moon stays in the middle, and the timeline along the bottom covers the next thirty days.
Step one, Site. Pick a landing site from the list, search by name, type in coordinates, or tap one of the best spots we found for the coming month.
On the Moon, the gold line points to the Sun from your site, and the blue line points to Earth. The pill at the top tells you, live, whether you have power and a radio link.
Step two, Date. The calendar colours every day for your site. Green means sunlight and Earth together for at least three days. Amber is power only. Red means no sunlight. Tap a day to choose it.
Not sure? Find the next good date searches the coming year for you.
Step three, Check. You get a clear verdict at touchdown, with one light for power and one for Earth contact, and the full assessment underneath.
Press Play, or drag along the timeline, to watch the Sun circle the sky, and see exactly when power and radio come and go.
Step four, What if. Move the site by a kilometre or shift the date by a day, and it tells you in plain words what changes.
For bigger questions, open the Compare Lab. It ranks your plans, shows how far each one is from your baseline, and charts every measure side by side.
Step five, Report. Your whole scenario on one page, ready to print, save as a PDF, or share as a link.
And if you're ever stuck, just ask Lumi. Type a question in plain English, and Lumi works out the answer with the same engine.
The tutorial, the tour, and your settings are always in the top right. Happy landing!
